chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Hammad ibn Uthman who said: Muhammad ibn Hakim narrated to me saying, 'I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying:'
The combining of the two salats is when there are no optional prayers between the two; but if there are optional prayers between the two, then there is no combining.

key_terms.الصَّلَاتَيْنِ: the two salats — either Dhuhr and Asr, or Maghrib and Isha
key_terms.الْجَمْعُ: combining (jam'), the practice of performing two obligatory prayers consecutively
key_terms.تَطَوُّعٌ: voluntary/optional prayers (nafl), which if inserted between the two obligatory prayers invalidates the combining

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on combining two salats (jam' al-salatayn) according to Imam al-Kazim?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a chain ending with Muhammad ibn Hakim who heard it directly from Imam Abu al-Hasan (likely Imam al-Kazim, the 7th Imam), establishes the ruling on combining the Dhuhr-Asr or Maghrib-Isha prayers (jam' al-salatayn). The Imam clarifies that combining two prayers is valid when no voluntary (nafl) prayers are performed between them; if one inserts nafl prayers between the two obligatory prayers, the combining is invalidated. This ruling reflects an important jurisprudential distinction in Shia fiqh regarding the conditions under which combining prayers is permissible.
